arguments.content:
CXX       := clang++
CXXFLAGS  := -std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Iinclude
LDFLAGS   :=

TARGET    := epilog
BUILD_DIR := build

SRCS_INTERNALS := $(wildcard internals/*.cpp)
SRCS_PARSER    := $(wildcard parser/*.cpp)
SRCS_ENGINE    := $(wildcard engine/*.cpp)
SRCS_ROOT      := main.cpp repl.cpp

OBJS_INTERNALS := $(patsubst internals/%.cpp, $(BUILD_DIR)/internals/%.o, $(SRCS_INTERNALS))
OBJS_PARSER    := $(patsubst parser/%.cpp,    $(BUILD_DIR)/parser/%.o,    $(SRCS_PARSER))
OBJS_ENGINE    := $(patsubst engine/%.cpp,    $(BUILD_DIR)/engine/%.o,    $(SRCS_ENGINE))
OBJS_ROOT      := $(patsubst %.cpp,           $(BUILD_DIR)/%.o,            $(SRCS_ROOT))

ALL_OBJS := $(OBJS_INTERNALS) $(OBJS_PARSER) $(OBJS_ENGINE) $(OBJS_ROOT)

.PHONY: all release debug clean

all: release

release: CXXFLAGS += -O2 -DNDEBUG
release: $(TARGET)

debug: CXXFLAGS += -g -O0 -DDEBUG
debug: $(TARGET)

$(TARGET): $(ALL_OBJS)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $^ -o $@ $(LDFLAGS)

$(BUILD_DIR)/internals/%.o: internals/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/parser/%.o: parser/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/engine/%.o: engine/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: %.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR) $(TARGET) $(TARGET).exe

@echo off
setlocal enabledelayedexpansion

set CXX=clang++
set CXXFLAGS=-std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Iinclude
set TARGET=epilog.exe

set MODE=release
if "%1"=="debug" (
    set MODE=debug
    set CXXFLAGS=%CXXFLAGS% -g -O0 -DDEBUG
) else (
    set CXXFLAGS=%CXXFLAGS% -O2 -DNDEBUG
)

if not exist build\internals mkdir build\internals
if not exist build\parser    mkdir build\parser
if not exist build\engine    mkdir build\engine

set SRCS=
for %%f in (main.cpp repl.cpp)     do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"
for %%f in (internals\*.cpp)       do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"
for %%f in (parser\*.cpp)          do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"
for %%f in (engine\*.cpp)          do set SRCS=!SRCS! "%%f"

echo [build] Compiling with clang++ (%MODE%)...
%CXX% %CXXFLAGS% %SRCS% -o %TARGET%

if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
    echo [build] clang++ failed, retrying with clang-cl...
    set CLFLAGS=/std:c++20 /W4 /EHsc /Iinclude
    if "%MODE%"=="debug" (
        set CLFLAGS=!CLFLAGS! /Od /Zi /DDEBUG
    ) else (
        set CLFLAGS=!CLFLAGS! /O2 /DNDEBUG
    )
    clang-cl !CLFLAGS! %SRCS% /Fe:%TARGET%
    if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
        echo [build] Both compilers failed.
        exit /b 1
    )
)

echo [build] Done: %TARGET%
endlocal

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

CXX=clang++
CXXFLAGS="-std=c++23 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Iinclude"
TARGET=epilog

MODE=${1:-release}
if [[ "$MODE" == "debug" ]]; then
    CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -g -O0 -DDEBUG"
else
    CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -O2 -DNDEBUG"
fi

mkdir -p build/internals build/parser build/engine

SRCS=(main.cpp repl.cpp)
mapfile -d '' -O "${#SRCS[@]}" SRCS < <(
    find internals parser engine -name '*.cpp' -print0
)

echo "[build] Compiling with clang++ ($MODE)..."
if $CXX $CXXFLAGS "${SRCS[@]}" -o "$TARGET"; then
    echo "[build] Done: $TARGET"
else
    echo "[build] clang++ failed, retrying with clang-cl..."
    clang-cl /std:c++20 /W4 /EHsc /Iinclude /O2 /DNDEBUG "${SRCS[@]}" /Fe:"$TARGET"
    echo "[build] Done: $TARGET"
fi

arguments.content:
# Epilog

> *The next evolutionary step after Prolog.*

Epilog is a logic programming runtime written in **C++23**, inspired by Prolog and designed from the ground up for modern hardware: multicore CPUs, incremental reasoning, predictive execution, and database-backed fact storage.

It is not a Prolog rewrite. It is what comes after.

---

## Status

**Version 0.1 — Minimal Prolog Runtime** (current)

A working interactive REPL with facts, rules, unification, backtracking, and a core set of built-in predicates. The foundation everything else is built on.

---

## Quick Start

### Build

**Windows:**
```bat
build.bat
```

**Linux / macOS:**
```sh
bash build.sh
```

**Make:**
```sh
make          # release build  (-O2)
make debug    # debug build    (-g -O0)
```

Requires `clang++` 21+ with C++23 support. Falls back to `clang-cl` on Windows if `clang++` fails.

### Run

**Interactive REPL:**
```bat
run.bat
```
```sh
bash run.sh
```
or directly:
```sh
./epilog
```

**Load a file then start the REPL:**
```sh
./epilog facts.pl
```

**Verbose / debug tracing:**
```sh
./epilog --verbose
./epilog -v facts.pl
```
Logs every resolution step, clause lookup, and unification result to stderr.

---

## The Language (Prolog subset)

### Facts

```prolog
parent(alice, bob).
parent(bob, carol).
```

### Rules

```prolog
grandparent(X, Y) :-
    parent(X, Z),
    parent(Z, Y).
```

### Queries

```prolog
?- grandparent(alice, carol).
```
```
true ;
```

```prolog
?- parent(X, Y).
```
```
X = alice
Y = bob ;
```

### Loading a file

From the REPL:
```prolog
consult('my_facts.pl').
```

Or on startup:
```sh
./epilog my_facts.pl
```

### Exiting

```prolog
halt.
```

---

## Built-in Predicates (v0.1)

| Predicate | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `true/0` | Always succeeds |
| `fail/0` | Always fails |
| `false/0` | Alias for `fail/0` |
| `!/0` | Cut — discard remaining choice points |
| `=/2` | Unification: `X = Y` |
| `\=/2` | Non-unification: succeeds if `X` and `Y` cannot unify |
| `write/1` | Print a term to stdout |
| `nl/0` | Print a newline |
| `assert/1` | Add a clause to the database (assertz semantics) |
| `assertz/1` | Alias for `assert/1` |
| `retract/1` | Remove the first matching clause |

---

## Architecture

```
epilog/
├── include/           Headers (.hpp) — shared across all layers
│   ├── atoms.hpp      Atom interning table
│   ├── variables.hpp  Logic variable registry + TermRef/VarId typedefs
│   ├── terms.hpp      Term representation (atom, var, int, compound)
│   ├── lexer.hpp      Tokenizer
│   ├── parser.hpp     Clause and query parser
│   ├── database.hpp   Clause store
│   ├── unifier.hpp    Robinson unification + Trail
│   ├── solver.hpp     Backtracking SLD resolution engine
│   ├── builtins.hpp   Built-in predicate dispatch
│   ├── repl.hpp       Read-Eval-Print Loop
│   └── log.hpp        Verbose logging (--verbose flag)
│
├── internals/         Core data structures
│   ├── atoms.cpp      FNV-1a hash table, open addressing, O(1) lookup
│   ├── variables.cpp  Per-query variable registry with Trail undo
│   └── terms.cpp      Arena allocator — no malloc after init
│
├── parser/            Language frontend
│   ├── lexer.cpp      Single-pass tokenizer, no backtracking
│   └── parser.cpp     Iterative top-down parser, no C recursion
│
├── engine/            Inference backend
│   ├── database.cpp   Predicate-indexed clause store
│   ├── unifier.cpp    Iterative unification with explicit work stack
│   ├── solver.cpp     Goal stack + choice-point stack, no C recursion
│   └── builtins.cpp   Dispatch table for built-in predicates
│
├── repl.cpp           Interactive REPL, file loader
└── main.cpp           Entry point, CLI argument handling
```

### Key Design Decisions

**C++23, not C.**
The codebase was originally C11 and converted to C++23. Benefits: `constexpr` constants instead of `#define`, `nullptr` instead of `NULL`, `static_cast` instead of C casts, scoped enums, aggregate initialisation, and `bool` instead of `int` for predicate returns. The JPL safety constraints (no post-init heap, bounded loops, no C-stack recursion) are retained.

**No heap allocation after init.**
Every subsystem uses a fixed-size arena or table declared at startup. `new`/`malloc` are never called during query execution. This follows JPL Rule 3 and makes memory behaviour fully predictable.

**No C-stack recursion in the engine.**
The unifier uses an explicit `UnifyPair` work stack. The solver uses an explicit `GoalStack` and `ChoiceStack`. `rename_term` recurses only over compound arity (bounded by `TERM_MAX_ARITY = 255`). This follows JPL Rule 1.

**Separate arenas for clauses and queries.**
Clause terms (asserted facts and rules) live in a persistent `clause_arena`. Each query gets its own `query_arena` that is reset between queries. Stored `TermRef` indices into `clause_arena` remain stable across queries.

**Variable names stored in Term nodes.**
Each `TERM_KIND_VAR` node carries its source-level name (`char name[64]`). The solver reads names directly from clause-arena term nodes when creating fresh renamed variables for each clause application — no dependency on a stale variable registry.

**`TermRef` bindings via `TERM_TERMREF` tag.**
Variables are bound to `TermRef` indices (into the query arena) rather than splitting into atom-bindings and var-bindings. This lets `deref` follow any binding — atom, integer, or compound — through a single uniform path.

---

## JPL Coding Standard Compliance

All source files follow the [NASA/JPL Institutional Coding Standard](https://yurichev.com/mirrors/C/JPL_Coding_Standard_C.pdf):

| Rule | How it is applied |
|------|------------------|
| **1** — No goto\*, no recursion | Engine uses explicit `GoalStack`/`ChoiceStack`; unifier uses a `UnifyPair` work stack |
| **2** — Fixed loop bounds | Every loop is bounded by a named `constexpr` capacity constant |
| **3** — No post-init dynamic allocation | All storage is pre-declared in fixed-size structs; no `new`/`malloc` during inference |
| **4** — Short functions | No function exceeds ~60 lines |
| **5** — Check all parameters and return values | Every public function validates inputs; callers check return codes |
| **6** — Preprocessor for includes and constants only | All constants are `constexpr`; no token pasting |
| **7** — Pointer depth ≤ 1 | No `**` in public APIs; all access through flat index types (`TermRef`, `VarId`, `AtomId`) |
| **8** — All warnings enabled | Built with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic` |

\* `goto` is used in `solver.cpp` for the backtracking label — it does not jump across any variable initialisations, satisfying C++ legality. The alternatives (recursive lambda, exception, setjmp) are worse under JPL rules.

---

## Roadmap

| Version | Goal | Status |
|---------|------|--------|
| **0.1** | Minimal Prolog runtime — facts, rules, unification, backtracking, REPL | **Done** |
| 0.2 | Indexing and caching — first-argument indexing, query statistics | Planned |
| 0.3 | Reactive reasoning — dependency graph, incremental recomputation | Planned |
| 0.4 | Database integration — SQLite-backed persistent facts | Planned |
| 0.5 | Graph reasoning — Neo4j integration, relationship traversal | Planned |
| 0.6 | Predictive execution — speculative cache, query pattern learning | Planned |
| 0.7 | Multicore reasoning — parallel branch exploration | Planned |
| 1.0 | Stable release | Planned |

See [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) for the detailed task breakdown per phase.

---

## Core Invariant

> Predictions, caching, and speculative execution never alter facts, rules, or logical conclusions.
> The inference engine is always the source of truth.

---

## Name

*Prolog* means "programming in logic."
*Epilog* is what comes after.
